sections.h2: Which Franklin office files Macon County deeds?
sections.html:
Macon County deeds go on the record at the county Register of Deeds office in Franklin. Macon County government works from 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734, and the county switchboard at (828) 349-2000 can connect you to the Register of Deeds.

The county directory lists a vault line and several extensions for the office. Ask the office for its recording hours and its same-day cutoff before you plan a closing around it.

The Register of Deeds is elected by county voters for a two-year term under G.S. 161-1. The office applies the same statewide recording rules used in all North Carolina counties, so a Macon County deed follows the same format, fee and tax rules as a deed filed elsewhere.

sections.h2: What do recording fees and the excise tax cost in Macon County?
sections.html:
Fees come from G.S. 161-10, and the excise tax comes from G.S. 105-228.30. The register collects both before a deed is recorded.

  • Ordinary instruments: a $26 base for up to 15 pages, with $4 for each page past that.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: a $64 base for up to 35 pages, again $4 for each extra page.
  • Satisfactions and cancellations of mortgages and deeds of trust: no fee.
  • A second instrument in the same document: $10.
  • Excise tax: $1 per $500 of value, rounded up for any partial block.

The seller is the transferor and owes the excise tax. The money splits two ways: the county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest goes to state revenue officials monthly, net of refunds and the county's allowance. Closing attorneys in Franklin normally deduct the tax from the seller's proceeds and deliver it with the deed.

sections.h2: Why does filing order matter to a Macon County seller?
sections.html:
Filing sets priority. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from deeds, sale contracts, options and leases over three years until they are registered where the land lies, and whoever registers first comes first.

A parcel that has passed through several families can carry old rights of way or boundary agreements. Have the closing attorney search the Macon County index for each prior owner, and ask the Land Records office for the parcel map so the legal description on the new deed matches the tax parcel.

Filing a deed does not itself clear the tax bill. The county assesses property as of January 1, so ask the tax office who is billed for the current year and plan the proration with your closing attorney.

sections.h2: What does the Macon County Land Records office do?
sections.html:
The Land Records office, also called the Mapping Office, is on the main level of the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in downtown Franklin. It is the place to get property cards, parcel maps and county maps, and it has public terminals for document searches, property searches, collection information and assessment data.

The tax office also links an address change form, property tax forms and a land records search from its page, so many owners can pull a map or a parcel record before they visit. A seller preparing a listing can print the parcel map to check the lot lines against the deed.

The Tax Department itself sits in the annex at 5 West Main Street. It posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the county scroll.

sections.h2: Which Macon County dates matter after I record a deed?
sections.html:
The county tax calendar drives most of what follows a sale. The Macon County Tax Department lists these dates on its home page.

Important dates listed by the Macon County Tax Department
DateWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment; personal property ownership and place of taxation are set as of this date
January 1 to 31Listing period for personal property, except tagged motor vehicles, and for exemption and exclusion filing
January 5Last day to pay property taxes without interest
January 6Interest begins
AprilReview board hears appeals
April 15Last date to file listings with a prior approved extension
AugustCurrent-year tax bills processed and mailed

The 2026 board began meeting April 7, 2026 and adjourned April 17, 2026, and appeals had to be received or postmarked by that day. The tax office also notes a 2027 reappraisal and offers an online appeal portal, so check there after any new values are mailed.

sections.h2: How do Macon County owners pay a tax bill, and what scam warning applies?
sections.html:
The county moved to a new bill-pay platform, and owners must register their accounts again and re-enroll in paperless billing. The portal runs around the clock and offers AutoPay, text alerts with pay-by-text, and an automated pay-by-phone line. The collections office answers at (828) 349-2142.

The tax office also posts a warning about lookalike government scams. It says the Macon County Tax Office does not contact taxpayers asking to come to their homes to collect a debt, and it tells residents not to share personal information and to hang up at once. Sellers who owe back taxes are a likely target for calls like that, so route any demand through the official office and your closing attorney.

Businesses must list business personal property each January under G.S. 105-308, which covers furniture, fixtures, machinery and similar equipment. A rental owner who keeps furnishings in an income-producing unit should ask the Personal Property desk at (828) 349-2144 whether those items need listing.

sections.h2: What is Macon County like for home sellers?
sections.html:
Macon County is a county whose communities include Franklin, Highlands and Nantahala. County population reached 39,232 in July 2025, a 6.0 percent rise from the 2020 base, across 515.58 square miles of land.

  • Persons 65 and over: 31.7 percent.
  • Housing units: 27,700, against 18,406 households for 2020 to 2024.
  • Persons per household: 2.04.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.6 percent.
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $251,900.
  • Typical rent: $803; household income at the midpoint: $59,061 in 2024 dollars.
  • Accommodation and food services sales: $205,516 thousand in 2022.

Those figures show more housing units than households. A buyer who plans a second home or a rental will want to see the recorded deed and any restrictions on file with the register.

sections.h2: What if the Macon County owner has died?
sections.html:
Call the clerk of superior court before the register of deeds. The directory lists the Estates and Special Proceedings line at (828) 349-7204, and that office can explain whether a small estate affidavit fits or whether the estate needs a personal representative.

For intestate estates, G.S. 28A-25-1 permits an affidavit filed with the clerk in the county of domicile when personal property less liens does not exceed $20,000, any time after 30 days from death. A surviving spouse who is the only heir may reach a limit up to $30,000 after the spousal allowance. The affidavit lists each tract of land the person owned.

When someone has authority to sign, the deed then goes to the Register of Deeds. Bring the certified death record if the register or the title company asks for it.

faqs.q: Where is the Macon County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is part of Macon County government in Franklin, whose main address is 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734. Call (828) 349-2000 and ask for the Register of Deeds to confirm hours.

faqs.q: What do Macon County deed filings cost?
faqs.a: An ordinary instrument starts at $26 for up to 15 pages, with $4 per page after that, and the excise tax adds $1 per $500 of value. The office collects both before it records the deed.

faqs.q: Does Macon County have a separate tax scroll for Highlands?
faqs.a: Yes, the Macon County Tax Department posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the main county scroll. Ask the tax office which scroll applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: When do Macon County property taxes become late?
faqs.a: January 5 is the last day to pay clear of interest, which starts January 6. Current-year bills are processed and mailed in August.

faqs.q: Where can I get a parcel map in Macon County?
faqs.a: Visit the Land Records office in the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in Franklin, or use the land records search linked from the tax office page. Property cards, parcel maps and county maps are available there.
